extracted.intended_audience: news readers and journalism professionals interested in newsroom ethics and verification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and lessons for newsroom verification, editorial oversight, hiring/vetting, and handling fabricated reporting, drawn from the Janet Cooke/'Jimmy's World' scandal and the Post ombudsman review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough reporter background checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post gave only a 'cursory' background check to Ms. Cooke; the 'usual check of references was done in a cursory manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify resume claims (education, foreign study, languages, prior employment) carefully rather than performing cursory checks; confirm references and credentials before hiring and before assigning sensitive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial verification of facts and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The jugular of journalism lay exposed -- the faith an editor has to place in a reporter' and 'This business of trusting reporters absolutely goes too far.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must independently corroborate reporters' facts and source claims instead of relying solely on a reporter's account; establish procedures for fact-checking and verification prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution when promising source anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: A key turning point was when Ms. Cooke was promised anonymity for her sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promises of anonymity should not substitute for verification; anonymous sourcing increases the need for corroboration and editorial scrutiny because it limits direct confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take internal doubts and concerns seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff members who doubted the story either kept their own counsel, or saw their reservations dismissed as jealousy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create channels and a culture that encourages reporters and editors to raise concerns and ensures those concerns are investigated rather than dismissed or stigmatized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist pressure for sensational, front‑page material
rubrics_metrics.description: Intense newsroom pressure for sensational, page one material blinds management to necessary caution and may inspire reporters to stretch the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize accuracy and verification over chasing sensational content; guard editorial processes against incentives that reward speed or shock at the expense of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present composite figures as real people
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's central subject, 'Jimmy,' was exposed as a 'composite' figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composites or amalgams are used for reporting purposes, disclose that fact clearly; never present composites as single real individuals without attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared accountability across the editorial chain
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There's enough blame to go around' — the ombudsman named executive and managing editors and others as responsible in the systems failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear responsibilities and accountability for verification at every editorial level; managers and editors share responsibility for preventing and detecting fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use independent/internal review and transparency after failures
rubrics_metrics.description: As ombudsman, Bill Green reviewed the incident, was 'invited' to do so, and received full cooperation from staff; the Post publicly accounted for returning the Pulitzer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ ombudsmen or independent reviews to investigate serious editorial failures, publish findings, and take visible corrective actions to restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough reference and credential checking (distinct from cursory checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive editor Bradlee was impressed by claimed credentials (Vassar, Sorbonne, languages) and 'the usual check of references was done in a cursory manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute robust reference-checking protocols for hires and for reporters whose work depends on personal credibility; verify educational and employment claims directly when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication follow-up, correction, and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence included the exposure of fabrication, Ms. Cooke's resignation, and the return of the Pulitzer the story had won.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fabrication or major errors are discovered, promptly correct the public record, issue retractions or returns of awards as appropriate, and explain remedial steps taken to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure hiring diversity goals do not override vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may have granted her a job speedily because of minority hiring pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue diversity in hiring while maintaining rigorous vetting and standards; avoid accelerating hiring decisions for demographic reasons at the expense of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish robust systems to prevent single-point failures
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It was a complete systems failure, and there's no excuse for it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design editorial workflows and checks so that no single individual's credibility or claims can bypass verification; build multiple safeguards and cross-checks into reporting and editing processes.
